news.title: Croatian football takeover underway in the United Arab Emirates
news.lede: The United Arab Emirates wants to reach the 2030 World Cup. To get there, it has turned to Croatia. As the UAE begins building towards the 2030 FIFA World Cup, it has placed its trust and gone all in on a group of coaches. Zlatko Dalić, Igor Bišćan and Branko Ivanković have all been appointed important roles, creating an unusually strong Croatian presence at the heart of the UAE’s football project.

news.title: NZ Football pulls support for Infantino as FIFA President
news.lede: New Zealand Football has pulled its support for Gianni Infantino as FIFA President amid the fallout from the embattled executive's failed World Cup sell-off plan. NZ Football, which governs the game in Aotearoa, also called for an independent review of the steps taken during the plan's development. "After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust," it said in a statement. "NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all FIFA member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

news.title: Ghana clear major hurdle in bid to end 20-year World Cup absence
news.lede: Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens. Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens, showed great courage to come from behind and defeat Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 in Casablanca. This victory keeps their dream of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup alive. The match started badly for Ghana.

news.title: India football ‘closer than ever’ to overseas players representing the nation
news.lede: Dubai: A major development for Indian football is on the horizon, with the country’s football authorities increasingly confident that players of Indian heritage based in Europe could soon be eligible to represent the national team.. Current rules bar Indian-heritage footballers based overseas from representing the national team unless they give up their foreign passport.. The rules have so far denied Indian footballers living abroad the chance to earn international caps and help the country climb back into the FIFA top 100.. However, one senior official told Sky Sports News he is “convinced” the way will soon be cleared for eligible overseas-based players to represent India..

news.title: Josephine Bonsu magic keeps Ghana’s World Cup dream alive
news.lede: When push comes to shove, teams need their best players to step up to the occasion. And for Ghana, that was defender Josephine Bonsu who converted a penalty from the spot to give the Black Queens a 2-1 victory over neighbours Côte d’Ivoire at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium in Casablanca on a cool Thursday night. With their title campaign down the drain at the TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, the Black Queens who were bronze medalists at last year’s edition, came into the game desperate to stay in the run for a spot at the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 in Brazil. The last time Ghana competed at the global stage was 2007.

news.title: VAR, timewasting and subs - new rules for the new season
news.lede: Michael Oliver is the Premier League's number one referee after Anthony Taylor announced his retirement. The 2026-27 season will feature an unprecedented number of new laws, mostly designed to tackle tempo disruption and make the game quicker. These rules were all initially rolled out at the World Cup, but still caused confusion in the first round of the Carabao Cup last weekend. These changes will be deployed right through English football, from the EFL kick off this weekend, Sunday's Community Shield between Arsenal and Manchester City, to the Premier League and right down to Sunday league - apart from the video assistant referee (VAR), of course.

news.title: Continental clash: where world football stands on Fifa and Infantino – explained
news.lede: With Oceania praising Fifa on Friday, all six confederations have finally had their say on the fallout from the World Cup sell-off plan. The Oceania Football Confederation’s (OFC) decision to belatedly issue a statement following this week’s executive committee meeting praising Fifa’s “progress achieved over the last decade” means all six continental confederations have finally had their say on the fallout from the World Cup sell-off plan that has split world football, with the votes seeming tied at three apiece on the key issue of whether Gianni Infantino should remain as Fifa president.
